$comment: Chronicler seat permission profile. APPLIED 2026-08-05 by edict. *** THE SEAT HAS NO STAGING ROOT AND THEREFORE NO WRITE SURFACE FOR ITS OWN OUTPUT. *** The draft carried a literal PLACEHOLDER-STAGING-ROOT path; the Overseer directed that it must never be applied as written, so the 3 staging-root allow rules were REMOVED rather than guessed at. Until he names the staging root (fortkit-zud.8) the Chronicler can read, reproduce, file beads and emit events, and cannot write a draft anywhere. That is the safe failure and it is deliberate. Security-publication seat permission profile. Drafted by the Regent under edict 2026-08-04; gate 1 applies. Modeled on herald-settings.json, but the envelope is deliberately WIDER in one direction and NARROWER in another. Wider: this seat must READ every fort's internals and RUN reproductions, which the Herald must never do (his safety property is that the digest is his only window). Narrower: this seat may never reach the outside world with a write. Layering is unchanged: this profile is policy, the kernel mask (fort/scripts/lib/seat-sandbox.sh) is the boundary, and the same verified caveat holds as for the Warden and Herald profiles: absent commands are not reliably denied, and deny rules bind a command SPELLING rather than a file (ForgeOs-21f.8, measured six-for-six). Treat allow as convenience, deny as intent, and the mask as the actual boundary. HANDOFF FIX 2026-08-05, found by Ilva Trueglass reading under 8.3: the profile allowed Write(civ/handoffs/*.md) and also denied Write(//home/justin/dev/**), which contains it. Deny beats allow, so a duty the covenant imposes at section 10 — every session writes a handoff — was impossible. The blanket deny is replaced by specific denies over product code, every fort tree, and the civ constitution and annals. He can now write his own handoff and nothing else. Note this makes the no-staging-root state visible rather than accidental: he still cannot write a draft, because no staging root has been named.
